prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1260; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas, where a vehicle operated by Driver 1 was struck from behind by a vehicle operated by Driver 2. Driver 1 was stopped at a signalized intersection when the impact occurred. A passenger was seated in the front seat of Driver 1's vehicle and was also in the vehicle when officers arrived, a fact confirmed by both drivers and the responding officers. Driver 1 reported a wrist injury and was transported for evaluation. The reported injury is consistent with the type and force of this collision. Damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle is largely in line with the described impact, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known to officers. Scene photographs confirm several details reported by the drivers. No independent witnesses were located at the scene. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the applicable auto policy.
